title: Oscar and the Alibi
premise: Vesper Almeida, the concierge of the Hotel Marlowe, has spent seven years cataloguing the secrets of the small town of Bellhaven—until she finds the diary of Oscar Renner, a guest who vanished three years ago, with entries written after his disappearance. Following the diary's coded references, she discovers that Oscar faked his death to escape a powerful family's crimes, and that his 'alibi' is a ledger hidden in the hotel itself, recording every bribe and body they buried. As the family closes in on her, Vesper must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the innocent people entangled in it, ending with her publishing the ledger, watching the guilty fall, and finally stepping out from behind the front desk into a life that is no longer invisible.
about_author: Rafael Joubert is the pen name of a former night auditor at a grand seaside hotel, where he collected a decade of overheard confessions and unsolved disappearances. He writes mysteries from a rented room above a laundromat, insisting that every plot he invents is less strange than what guests actually confess at 3 a.m.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Strangers
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. In her meticulous card-file of guest secrets, Vesper notices an anomaly: Oscar Renner's room was never checked out, yet his bill kept being paid for months after his disappearance. The emotional beat is quiet unease—the first crack in seven years of comfortable invisibility.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Cleaning out the sealed room, she finds Oscar's diary behind a wall panel; its final entries are dated weeks after police declared him dead. The beat is vertigo: the dead do not write, so either Oscar lives or someone wants the town to think he does.

chapters.title: What the Desk Hears
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. She quietly interviews staff and old regulars, learning Oscar had grown paranoid about the Calloway family before vanishing. The beat is mounting dread as she realizes her own archive may have helped someone track him.

chapters.title: A Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Deciphering the diary's references to room numbers and dates, she recognizes them as the hotel's own historical occupancy records—a ledger of Calloway bribes and cover-ups disguised as bookings. The beat is electrifying clarity.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Left
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Vesper and diary entries. A stranger checks in asking pointed questions about Oscar; Vesper lies smoothly for the first time in her career. The beat is fear sharpening into resolve—she is no longer a bystander.

chapters.title: Loyalty on Credit
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Her oldest friend, the hotel's longtime manager, warns her to stop—and she realizes he has been taking Calloway money for years. The beat is heartbreak: loyalty and truth pull in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Room 314
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Following the ledger's final entry, she finds evidence hidden in Room 314—and a living, frightened Oscar Renner, hiding in the town under a new name. The beat is shock and wary alliance: the ghost is real and terrified.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar (with Vesper present). Oscar confesses why he ran: he witnessed a Calloway killing and chose silence to stay alive, and the diary was his slow act of courage. The beat is shame meeting compassion.

chapters.title: Checkout Time
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. The Calloways corner her in the hotel, demanding the ledger; the manager must finally choose a side, buying her time at great cost. The climax beat is courage under threat as Vesper refuses to hand over the truth.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. The ledger reaches a journalist and the police; arrests follow, Oscar testifies, and the manager accepts his reckoning. Vesper resigns from the desk, her file of secrets closed at last. The final beat is liberation: she steps into daylight, seen.
